records.text: Aleister Crowley hosted occult sex-magic parties around the world
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: It's right there in your face. If you just look into history a tiny bit and Aleister Crowley, who was once termed the world's wickedest man, would host these parties all across the world.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Scholarly histories document Crowley's sexual-magick practices and international occult networks, but do not establish the episode's sweeping formulation that he hosted occult sex-magic parties 'across the world.'

sources.title: The Sorcerer and His Apprentice
sources.relevance: Scholarly history of Crowley's magical practice and Abbey.

records.text: Aleister Crowley created the religion of Thelema and attempted to summon demons in France
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And he even created his own religion around it, religion of Thelema, Black magic. There are so many stories out there regarding Aleister Crowley attempting to summon various demons in France. He tried to summon Pan, I think, in Paris.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Current scholarly references confirm Crowley developed Thelema, but the specific claim that he attempted to summon demons in France was not corroborated by the sources located.

sources.title: Aleister Crowley (1875-1947)
sources.relevance: Academic reference entry on Crowley and Thelema.

records.text: A 23-year-old Oxford student whom Aleister Crowley regarded as his magical heir went to Sicily with him and died
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This was a 23-year-old student, okay? Aleister Crowley thinks he has. The it factor, they go down to Sicily, and the kid ends up dead.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Historical sources identify 23-year-old Oxford undergraduate Raoul Loveday as a Crowley follower who went to the Abbey of Thelema in Sicily and died there in 1923.

sources.title: Rethinking Aleister Crowley and Thelema
sources.relevance: Scholarly account of Crowley's Abbey and Raoul Loveday.

records.text: Aleister Crowley believed he could make himself invisible and tried to bestow that power on Raoul Loveday
records.speaker: Ashley (Candace Owens producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: Yeah, so basically, Aleister Crowley was convinced that he was able to make himself invisible and he was trying to bestow that power upon his little magical heir, Raoul Loveday.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The invisibility-power account is presented as an occult anecdote; no reliable independent contemporary or scholarly source located substantiates Crowley bestowing such a power on Loveday.

records.text: Aleister Crowley and Raoul Loveday became seriously ill during a ceremony at Crowley’s abbey in Sicily
records.speaker: Ashley (Candace Owens producer; surname unverified)

appearances.snippet: This was during one of his infamous ceremonies at his abbey in Sicily. But during the experiment, they both got really sick.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Sources document Loveday's fatal illness, but no reliable source located corroborates that both men became seriously ill during an invisibility ceremony.

records.text: Benito Mussolini expelled Aleister Crowley from Italy for being a Satanist
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: OK, what ended up happening was Mussolini, the evil fascist, kicked him out of the country for being a Satanist.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Scholarship confirms Mussolini's government expelled Crowley from Italy in 1923 amid scandal surrounding the Abbey, but 'for being a Satanist' is not the documented official reason.

sources.title: The Sorcerer and His Apprentice
sources.relevance: Scholarly account confirms the 1923 expulsion amid sensational press coverage.

records.text: Pauline Robinson Pierce gave birth to Barbara Bush a little over eight and a half months after spending time with Aleister Crowley
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Mr. Crowley, eight and a half months later, she gives birth to Barbara Bush, okay? This is just, again, a little over eight and a half months after hanging out with Aleister Crowley.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Current fact-checking and Bush-family biographical records reject the Crowley-parentage story; no reliable evidence establishes the alleged meeting or conception timeline.

sources.relevance: Fact check rejects the Crowley-Barbara Bush parentage story.

records.text: The timing of Pauline Robinson Pierce’s contact with Aleister Crowley is the source of rumors that Crowley was Barbara Bush’s father
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Obviously, you know who Barbara Bush is, the mother of George Bush. Now, this is the source of the rumors that Barbara Bush is actually the child of Aleister Crowley.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Fact-check histories identify the alleged Crowley-Pauline contact/timing story as the basis of the Barbara Bush paternity rumor, while also finding the rumor unsupported.

records.text: Jack Parsons was Aleister Crowley’s protégé and conducted occult sex rituals intended to create a “moon child”
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That's the precursor to NASA's Apollo program. Oh, he was such a genius. Yes, he was trying to literally summon demons. He was Aleister Crowley's protege. He was doing the exact same thing that Aleister Crowley was doing, throwing elite sex parties, saying we're going to create a moon child, everyone sex, drugs.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. Reliable histories support that Parsons was a Crowley disciple and performed sex-magick/Babalon Working rituals; the episode's specific 'Moon Child' phrasing is interpretive rather than directly documented in the source located.

sources.title: Queer Correspondence
sources.relevance: Smithsonian history connects Parsons to Crowley and sex-magick practice.

records.text: Aleister Crowley created an entire religion, books, and pentacles meant to summon spirits.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This is how you build a matrix in effect, right? That is the reason why Aleister Crowley, who was a master occultist, created an entire religion around this, put together a series of books, a series of pentacles that are meant to summon various spirits.

verification.notes: Context reviewed at 13:48. Crowley founded Thelema and wrote or edited numerous occult works, including material on invocation and the Goetia. However, the claim compresses distinct facts: he did not originate every referenced spirit/pentacle tradition, and the Lesser Key/Goetia predates him.

sources.title: Thelema FAQ - Ordo Templi Orientis UK
sources.relevance: Confirms Crowley's central role in Thelema but not creation of the older pentacle and Goetic traditions.
